claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9457 s3.1.1: "Consumers MUST use the 'type' URI (after resolution, if necessary) as the problem type's primary identifier." Lesson s4 "RFC 9457 makes `type` the primary identifier of a problem type" matches.

RFC 9457 s3.1.3: "The 'title' member is a JSON string containing a short, human-readable summary of the problem type." ... "is advisory and is included only for users who are unaware of and cannot discover the semantics of the type URI."

RFC 9457 s3.1.4: "The 'detail' member is a JSON string containing a human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the problem." "Consumers SHOULD NOT parse the 'detail' member for information; extensions are more suitable and less error-prone ways to obtain such information."

RFC 9457 s3.1.1: "When this member is not present, its value is assumed to be 'about:blank'." s4.2.1: about:blank "indicates that the problem has no additional semantics beyond that of the HTTP status code."

RFC 9457 s3.2: "Problem type definitions MAY extend the problem details object with additional members that are specific to that problem type." "Clients consuming problem details MUST ignore any such extensions that they don't recognize."
